statement: What is the greatest value of $x$ that satisfies $7 - 2x \ge 3x + 22$?

choices.misconception: I combined $-2x$ and $3x$ into just $x$ instead of $5x$, so I got $7 - 22 \ge x$ and a greatest value of $-15$.
I added the 7 to the 22 instead of subtracting it, so I got $-29 \ge 5x$ and $x \le -\dfrac{29}{5}$.
I moved the numbers the wrong way and wrote $22 - 7 = 15 \ge 5x$, so I got $x \le 3$ and a greatest value of 3.

hints: Get all the $x$ terms on one side and all the numbers on the other.
Add $2x$ to both sides and subtract $22$ from both sides.
That gives $-15 \ge 5x$. Divide both sides by $5$.

solutions.reliable: Add $2x$ to both sides: $7 \ge 5x + 22$. Subtract $22$: $-15 \ge 5x$. Divide by $5$: $x \le -3$. The greatest value is $-3$. Check: $x = -3$ gives $7 + 6 = 13$ and $-9 + 22 = 13$, so equality holds.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
